en: It's for me; ser in the present, for he/she/it — this is what it is, not how it happens to be right now.
Is he here?; estar in the present, for he/she/it — how or where something is at the moment.
I'm fine; estar in the present, for I — how or where something is at the moment.
He still hasn't; haber in the present, for he/she/it — pairs with a past participle: *have* done.
Let's go already!; ir in the present, for we — also just means let's go.
Is there anything?; haber in the present, for he/she/it — used with no subject for there is or there are.
I don't have anything; tener in the present, for I — to have or hold.
How are you?; estar in the present, for you (tú) — how or where something is at the moment.
I don't know why; saber in the present, for I — to know a fact.
I already have; haber in the present, for I — pairs with a past participle: *have* done.
It has to be me; the plain form of ser, to be — what something is, not how it happens to be right now.
He has something of mine; tener in the present, for he/she/it — to have or hold.
I can't take any more; poder in the present, for I — to be able or allowed.
I don't want anything else; querer in the present, for I — want, or love, when it's a person.
I don't know what to do; the plain form of hacer, to do or to make.
It was all because of you; ser in the past, for he/she/it — it happened, it's over.
Thanks for everything; Feminine plural noun for thanks from gracia which alone means grace or wit.
Not again; Feminine noun for a time or occasion with plural veces.
He used to be like that; ser in the past, for he/she/it — that's how it was back then, over a stretch of time.
I'm not like that; ser in the present, for I — that's just who I am.
Are they for me?; ser in the present, for they — this is what it is, not how it happens to be right now.
What have you got there?; tener in the present, for you (tú) — to have or hold.
I think so; creer in the present, for I — to believe or think something.
I'm on my way there now; ir in the present, for I — to go or to be heading somewhere.
Do you know anything about him?; saber in the present, for you (tú) — to know a fact or piece of information.
It was here earlier; estar in the past, for he/she/it — that's how it was back then, over a stretch of time.
Could that be?; poder in the present, for he/she/it — puede ser is how you say "maybe".
You're just like that; ser in the present, for you (tú) — that's just who you are.
That isn't true; Feminine noun for truth and as ¿verdad? it tags a sentence.
Let's go to my place; Feminine noun for house or home, and en casa takes no article.
I don't have time; Masculine noun for time and also for the weather.
How's everything going?; ir in the present, for he/she/it — goes or is going.
Please don't; Masculine noun for a favour, fixed in the request por favor.
What do you want from me?; querer in the present, for you (tú) — want, or love, when it's a person.
I'm very sorry; sentir in the present, for I — to feel, and lo siento apologises.
Is the gentleman here?; Masculine noun for a gentleman or sir or Mr before a surname.
A long time ago; hacer in the present, for he/she/it — with a time span it means ago.
You have to do something; haber in the present, for you (tú) — pairs with a past participle: *have* done.
What do you mean?; the plain form of decir, to say or to tell.
We have to do something; tener in the present, for we — tener que means to have to.
Where is everybody?; estar in the present, for they — how or where something is at the moment.
Can you do that?; poder in the present, for you (tú) — to be able or allowed.
I can't see anything; the plain form of ver, to see.
Oh come on!; Masculine noun for a man and in Spain an exclamation of appeal.
That's life; Feminine noun for life and mi vida is an endearment.
There are lots of things; Feminine plural noun for things from singular cosa.
I have to go; the plain form of ir, to go — and ir a plus a plain verb is the future.
I'm ten years old; Masculine plural noun for years used with tener for age.
I want to be here; the plain form of estar, to be — how or where something is at the moment.
All day; Masculine noun for a day and masculine despite its final a.
I can't tonight; Feminine noun for night or evening with esta noche meaning tonight.
We're here now; estar in the present, for we — how or where something is at the moment.
I agree with you; Masculine noun for an agreement used in the phrase estar de acuerdo.
I don't have a job; Masculine noun for work or a job.
Sounds good to me; parecer in the present, for he/she/it — to seem or to look like.
There are a lot of people here; Feminine noun for people, and it takes a singular verb in Spanish.
Whatever works is fine; ser in the subjunctive (after wishes, doubt, hopes), for he/she/it — lo que sea means whatever.
My father isn't in; Masculine noun for father whose plural padres usually means parents.
Look at this; mirar as a command to one person (tú) — to look at or watch.
Who said that?; decir in the past, for he/she/it — to say or tell, it happened, it's over.
What do you want?; querer in the present, for you (polite, usted) — want, or love, when it's a person.
It could be; poder in the would-form, for I or he/she/it — could or might.
I want to talk to you; the plain form of hablar, to speak or talk.
Where are you going?; ir in the present, for you (tú) — vas a plus a plain verb is how you say the future.
What's going on?; pasar in the present, for he/she/it — to happen, to pass, or to spend time.
They have to talk to me; haber in the present, for they — pairs with a past participle: han hablado.
Do you have any money?; Masculine noun for money and uncountable so it has no plural.
I want to see the world; Masculine noun for world with todo el mundo meaning everybody.
One moment please; Masculine noun for a moment with en este momento meaning right now.
Can I have one?; the plain form of tener, to have or hold, with tener que meaning to have to.
I have been here; past participle of estar (the -ed form, pairs with haber), never changing its ending.
There were a lot of people; haber in the past, for he/she/it — there was or there were, always singular.
He didn't have any money; tener in the past, for I or he/she/it — that's how it was back then, over a stretch of time.
And your mother?; Feminine noun for mother though mamá is the usual term of address.
Okay see you tomorrow; valer in the present, for he/she/it — to be worth, and vale is Spain's everyday okay.
What place is this?; Masculine noun for a place with tener lugar meaning to take place.
What are you doing?; the -ing form of hacer, used with estar for doing or making right now.
Nobody knows anything; saber in the present, for he/she/it — to know a fact or how to do something.
We can go tomorrow; poder in the present, for we — to be able or may.
Hold on a second; esperar as a command to one person (tú) — to wait or hope.
What became of him?; past participle of ser (the -ed form, pairs with haber), as in ha sido, has been.
That's something else; Feminine noun for a thing with la cosa es que meaning the thing is.
How is your son?; Masculine noun for son whose plural hijos covers children of either sex.
What kind of man?; Masculine noun for a type or kind and informally a guy.
Are you his friend?; Masculine noun for a male friend with no romantic meaning.
Who is that woman?; Feminine noun for woman and also wife as in mi mujer.
Mom I'm coming; Feminine noun for mom the affectionate everyday word for one's mother.
Is dad home?; Masculine noun for dad the affectionate everyday word for one's father.
Three days ago; Masculine plural of día meaning days as in buenos días.
What does she say?; decir in the present, for he/she/it — to say, with dice que reporting what someone said.
I need to talk to you; necesitar in the present, for I — to need something.
I didn't say that; decir in the past, for I — it happened, it's over.
Hey have you got a minute?; oír as a command to one person (tú) — also used to grab attention.
I like this place; gustar in the present, for he/she/it — it means to be pleasing, so the thing you like is what does the acting.
I just wanted to see you; querer in the past, for I or he/she/it — wanting something, or a softer way to ask.
Can it be true?; ser in the future, for he/she/it — also used to guess that something probably is.
There might be something; the plain form of haber, giving there is after another verb as in puede haber.
Somewhere else; Feminine noun for a part with en alguna parte meaning somewhere.
What's your name?; Masculine noun for a name with a nombre de meaning in the name of.
What a mess!; Feminine noun for shit genuinely vulgar and used alone as a curse.
That must be true; deber in the present, for he/she/it — must or ought to before the plain form of a verb.
I haven't seen anything; irregular past participle of ver (the -ed form, pairs with haber), and it never changes shape.
I don't care at all; importar in the present, for he/she/it — to matter or be of concern.
They have a lot of money; tener in the present, for they — to have or hold.
We've seen everything; haber in the present, for we — pairs with a past participle: *have* done.
You're right; Feminine noun meaning reason, tener razón is to be right.
I want to know the truth; the plain form of saber, to know a fact or piece of information.
Who did this?; hacer in the past, for he/she/it — did or made, it happened, it's over.
Sometimes I don't know; Feminine plural of vez, times or occasions as in a veces.
They don't see anything; ver in the present, for they — to see.
I have no idea; Feminine noun for an idea, ni idea means no clue.
There's a problem; Masculine noun for a problem despite the final a.
What time is it?; Feminine noun for a clock hour or an appointment slot.
Love of my life; Masculine noun for love, mi amor is a common endearment.
He doesn't see well; ver in the present, for he/she/it — to see.
My whole family is here; Feminine noun for family, counts as singular so it takes a singular verb.
The police are here; Feminine noun where la policía is the force and un policía one officer.
I should go; deber in the would-form, for I — should or ought to.
That girl doesn't like me; Feminine noun for a girl or a young woman.
Let's go guys!; Masculine plural of chico, guys or kids including a mixed group.
He tells me everything; contar in the present, for he/she/it — to tell or to count.
What are you doing here?; hacer in the present, for you (tú) — to do or to make.
I want to get out of here; the plain form of salir, to leave or go out of a place.
What a problem!; ir in the subjunctive (after wishes, doubt, hopes), for he/she/it — also an exclamation meaning wow.
See you tomorrow; ver in the present, for I — to see.
They're my friends; Masculine plural of amigo, friends including women in a mixed group.
My brother is a police officer; Masculine noun for brother, the plural hermanos means siblings.
I thought he was my friend; pensar in the past, for I — thought or believed, it happened, it's over.
I didn't know anything about this; saber in the past, for I — knew or used to know, that's how it was back then, over a stretch of time.
I've got something in my head; Feminine noun for the head, also where ideas and sense sit.
Thanks sweetheart; Masculine noun for affection, also a term of endearment for anyone.
What do I say now?; decir in the present, for I — to say or to tell.
Where are you all going?; ir in the present, for they — to go.
Two men are here; Masculine plural of hombre, men or an interjection expressing surprise.
We're friends; ser in the present, for we — this is what it is, not how it happens to be right now.
That's no way to talk; Feminine noun for a shape or a way of doing something.
He's next to me; Masculine noun for a side, al lado de means beside.
I have to talk to you; deber in the present, for I — must, or with an object it means to owe.
It would be a problem; ser in the would-form, for he/she/it — would be.
In that case I'm not going; Masculine noun for a case, hacer caso means to pay attention.
You can go out; poder in the present, for they — can or be allowed to.
What happened?; pasar in the past, for he/she/it — happened or passed by, it's over.
That boy is my brother; Masculine noun for a boy or a young guy, also means small.
I didn't do anything; hacer in the past, for I — did or made, it happened, it's over.
There are a lot of people here; Feminine plural of persona, individual people you can count.
Is the lady of the house in?; Feminine noun for a married or older woman, also means wife.
I want to go back home; the plain form of volver, to return or with a plus another plain verb to do again.
Let's go along that path; Masculine noun for a road or path, en camino means on the way.
He's talking to my mother; the -ing form of hablar, talking and also used after seguir or ir.
No way; Feminine noun for a way or a method, de ninguna manera means no way.
Who is that person?; Feminine noun for a person and always feminine even about a man.
I need your help; Feminine noun for help and alone it is a shout for help.
Do you know this story?; Feminine noun covering both a story and history.
I was going to say something; ir in the past, for I or he/she/it — was going, back then over a stretch of time.
I suppose so; suponer in the present, for I — to suppose or assume.
I do not understand anything; entender in the present, for I — to understand.
Someone is at the door; Feminine noun for a door or a gate.
Do you see what I mean?; ver in the present, for you (tú) — to see.
Nothing is going to happen; the plain form of pasar, to happen or pass by or spend time.
What does that mean?; significar in the present, for he/she/it — to mean.
What day of the week is it?; Feminine noun for a week and fin de semana is the weekend.
I hope to see you today; esperar in the present, for I — to hope or wait or expect.
One more year here; Masculine noun for a year.
The kids are not here; Masculine plural of niño for children including mixed groups of boys and girls.
Hey man! What are you doing?; Masculine noun for an uncle and in Spain a casual dude.
You are so lucky!; Feminine noun for luck which you have with tener suerte.
We are going to another city; Feminine noun for a city with the plural ciudades.
He does not even know my name; Adverb paired with ni to mean not even.
Do you want to come with me?; the plain form of venir, to come toward the speaker.
My daughter is two years old; Feminine noun for a daughter.
I would like to talk with you; gustar in the would-form, for he/she/it — it would please me.
Wait five minutes; Masculine plural of minuto for minutes.
His father's death; Feminine noun for death despite the final -e.
Can you leave that here?; the plain form of dejar, to leave something or let someone do something.
Actually I do not know; Feminine noun for reality and en realidad means actually.
He does not stop talking; dejar in the present, for he/she/it — dejar de means stop doing something.
We have problems; Masculine plural of problema and masculine despite the final -a.
Nobody gives me anything; dar in the present, for he/she/it — to give.
My heart is yours; Masculine noun for a heart with the plural corazones.
I am scared; Masculine noun for fear which you have with tener miedo.
Where is the boss?; Masculine noun for a boss with la jefa for a woman.
I want a little water; Feminine noun for water though it takes el in the singular.
I have been waiting three hours; Feminine plural of hora for hours or clock time.
Power is everything; Masculine noun for power, and also the plain form of the verb poder.
My wife is at home; Feminine noun for a wife and in the plural also handcuffs.
Hands up!; Feminine plural of mano for hands and feminine despite the final -o.
You must see this; deber in the present, for you (tú) — must or ought to.
Is anyone else coming?; venir in the present, for he/she/it — to come toward the speaker.
Come on! Let's go!; venir in the subjunctive (after wishes, doubt, hopes), for he/she/it — also the polite command to one person.
She has her mother's eyes; Masculine plural of ojo for eyes and ¡Ojo! warns you to watch out.
I want to find a place; the plain form of encontrar, to find, with the stem change in encuentro.
Give me your hand; Feminine noun for a hand and feminine despite the final -o.
That boy is my son; Masculine noun for a small boy or child.
I do not want to see your face; Feminine noun for a face.
Careful with the water!; Masculine noun for care used in tener cuidado to be careful.
Three nights without you; Feminine plural of noche for nights as in buenas noches.
It is the end of the world; Masculine noun for an end and por fin means at last.
Shall we go for a drink?; the plain form of tomar, to take or to drink.
Listen to your mother; escuchar in the present, for he/she/it — also the command to one person (tú).
We are about to leave; Masculine noun for a point or dot or full stop.
Is he still here?; seguir in the present, for he/she/it — to follow, or to keep on being something.
I hope there is water; haber in the subjunctive (after wishes, doubt, hopes), for he/she/it — used after words that call for that mood.
My team is my family; Masculine noun for a team or the gear and kit for a job.
Your father needs help; necesitar in the present, for he/she/it — to need something.
What time are you going to arrive?; the plain form of llegar, to arrive — it takes a before the destination.
The doctor is already here; Masculine noun for a doctor and also a title of address.
If only there were time; haber in the past subjunctive, for he/she/it — for wishes that aren't real and if-clauses.
My car is at home; Masculine noun for a car and the everyday word in Spain.
What do I do now?; hacer in the present, for I — to do or to make.
I have class in the morning; Feminine noun for a class or lesson and also a kind or sort.
Why do you say that?; decir in the present, for you (tú) — to say or to tell.
What is your mother's name?; llamar in the present, for he/she/it — to call, and with se it means to be named.
Take my hand; tomar in the present, for he/she/it — to take or to drink, and the same form works as a command.
The earth is our home; Feminine noun for soil or land or the planet itself.
This war has no end; Feminine noun for war, and dar guerra means being a handful.
Let me think for a moment; the plain form of pensar, to think — pensar en is to think about something.
I hope she can come; poder in the subjunctive (after wishes, doubt, hopes), for he/she/it — to be able to do something.
There is blood in the water; Feminine noun for blood with no ordinary plural.
The women are here already; Plural of the feminine noun mujer meaning women and also wives.
Just one more lap; Feminine noun for a turn or a lap or the change from a payment.
It was me; ser in the past, for I — it happened, it's over, and the same form is shared with ir.
I don't want to work today; the plain form of trabajar, to work — trabajar en names the workplace.
I haven't had time; past participle of tener (the -ed form, pairs with haber), which never changes for gender.
I like this game; Masculine noun for a game or a match and also a set of things.
His body isn't well; Masculine noun for a body and also a corps of people.
Can I come in?; the plain form of entrar, to go in — it takes en or a before the place.
Nobody believes me; creer in the present, for he/she/it — to believe, and creer en is to believe in.
She couldn't speak; poder in the past, for he/she/it — an ongoing inability over a stretch of time, not one failed moment.
We have to go now; deber in the present, for we — must, and deber plus the plain form of a verb states an obligation.
Give me a chance; Feminine noun for a chance or an opening for something.
Where is my phone?; Masculine noun for a telephone and por teléfono means on the phone.
We need more time; necesitar in the present, for we — to need, and it takes its object directly.
In the end nothing happened; Masculine noun for an ending while la final is a championship match.
Are you going to the party?; Feminine noun for a party and also a public holiday.
Where were you last night?; estar in the past, for you (tú) — the normal past for where something was or how it was.
Everybody wants money; querer in the present, for they — to want, and with a it means to love a person.
My brother's car; Masculine noun for a car short for automóvil and usual in Latin America.
Can you give me something?; the plain form of dar, to give — it builds set phrases like dar miedo.
I want to live here; the plain form of vivir, to live — vivir de names what you live on.
My sister knows nothing; Feminine noun for a sister while the plural hermanos covers mixed siblings.
What's your number?; Masculine noun for a number and also a size or an issue.
Just two more months; Plural of the masculine noun mes meaning months and el mes que viene is next month.
It's not my fault; Feminine noun for fault or blame and tener la culpa is to be guilty.
The kids are at school; Feminine noun for a school usually the primary one.
He has already left; past participle of ir (the -ed form, pairs with haber), and with se it means having left.
What are you saying?; the -ing form of decir, used with estar for something happening right now.
Your boss talks a lot; hablar in the present, for he/she/it — to speak or talk to someone.
Maybe it's in the car; estar in the subjunctive (after wishes, doubt, hopes), for he/she/it — used after words of doubt like quizás.
I have a question; Feminine noun for a question and you hacer una pregunta rather than say one.
The girls are talking; Plural of the feminine noun chica meaning girls or young women.
Were they your friends?; ser in the past, for they — that's how people or things used to be back then, over a stretch of time.
What's going on?; pasar in the -ing form — to happen, to pass by, or to spend time.
Where is the captain?; Masculine noun for a captain, a ship's master or a team leader.
My sister has a baby; Masculine noun for a baby, it stays masculine even for a girl.
We don't know anything; saber in the present, for we — to know a fact or piece of information.
Do you like the food?; Feminine noun for food and also the main meal of the day.
I don't want to die; the plain form of morir, to die, the stem becomes ue in muero.
I don't know that man; conocer in the present, for I — to know or be acquainted with people.
Shall we go eat something?; the plain form of comer, to eat and often to have lunch.
A wine please; Masculine noun for wine, the drink made from grapes.
Do you have the list?; Feminine noun for a list, as an adjective it means ready or clever.
I want him to do it; hacer in the subjunctive (after wishes, doubt, hopes), for he/she/it — to do or make, required after querer que.
I have two children; Masculine plural of hijo, sons or children of both sexes.
My parents are here; Masculine plural of padre, usually the two parents together.
The room is ready; Feminine noun for a room, a bedroom or a hotel room.
I can't believe this; the plain form of creer, to believe or to think something true.
I'm thinking about you; pensar in the -ing form — to think, and pensar en means to think about.
It was two days; ser in the past, for they — it happened, it's over, a fact about identity.
What's it about?; tratar in the present, for he/she/it — to treat, and tratarse de means to be about.
I'm looking for you; buscar in the -ing form — to look for, and it takes no preposition.
I was never afraid; tener in the past, for I — to have, a state that started and finished.
I love you so much; amar in the present, for I — to love deeply.
You're very young; Adjective meaning young, also a noun for a young person of either sex.
A couple of hours; Masculine noun for a pair, un par de means a couple of.
What are they doing here?; hacer in the present, for they — to do or make.
We'll keep going like this; the plain form of seguir, to follow or to keep doing something.
What do they say?; decir in the present, for they — to say or tell.
I haven't got a clue; Feminine noun for a whore, most often a very crude intensifier.
They don't know anything; saber in the present, for they — to know facts or information.
It doesn't make sense; Masculine noun for meaning or sense and also a direction of travel.
Don't do that; hacer in the subjunctive (after wishes, doubt, hopes), for you (tú) — used for the negative command don't do.
We have to wait a bit; the plain form of esperar, to wait or to hope or to expect.
He has a weapon; Feminine noun for a weapon, it takes el in the singular.
That's five dollars; Masculine plural of dólar, dollars as money.
They were at the house; estar in the past, for they — that's how or where they were back then, over a stretch of time.
It's for your safety; Feminine noun for safety and security and also confidence.
He was here yesterday; estar in the past, for he/she/it — it happened, it's over, a finished stay somewhere.
Don't worry; preocupar in the subjunctive (after wishes, doubt, hopes), for you (tú) — no te preocupes means don't worry.
Give me your word; Feminine noun for a word and also a promise you give.
We're waiting for you; esperar in the -ing form — to wait for or to expect.
There's nothing left; quedar in the present, for he/she/it — to remain or be left.
Is he in his office?; Feminine noun for an office or a public bureau.
You can't kill anyone; the plain form of matar, to kill, the victim needs a personal a.
I'll go with you; ir in the future, for I — I will go.
The baby is in bed; Feminine noun for a bed as in irse a la cama.
I haven't heard anything; past participle of oír (the -ed form, pairs with haber), to hear, also the noun for ear.
There wouldn't be any problems; haber in the would-form, for he/she/it — there would be or would have.
Where can my phone be?; estar in the future, for he/she/it — often a guess about right now.
He gave me his number; dar in the past, for he/she/it — to give, and it's done.
It's a keepsake from my father; Masculine noun for a memory or a souvenir, recuerdos also sends regards.
He is not being fair; ser in the -ing form, used with estar for how someone is acting right now rather than who they are.
I hope he is right; tener in the subjunctive (after wishes, doubt, hopes), for he/she/it — also works as a polite command to one person.
There is no light here; Feminine noun for light, daylight, or electricity, with plural luces.
What the hell is he doing?; Plural of the masculine demonio, used as a mild swear after qué.
I want to sleep a bit; the plain form of dormir, to sleep — it changes its stem to duermo.
This is not his place; Masculine noun for a spot or seat, and un sitio web means website.
Can I help with something?; the plain form of ayudar, to help — it takes a personal a before people.
I have to get hold of some money; the plain form of conseguir, to obtain or manage after effort — the yo form is consigo.
My husband knows nothing; Masculine noun for husband, the everyday word in speech.
Leave me alone; Feminine noun for peace, and en paz means left alone.
I do not like your plan; Masculine noun for a plan, with plural planes.
He has given me his word; past participle of dar (the -ed form, pairs with haber), meaning given — it never changes after haber.
His father died yesterday; morir in the past, for he/she/it — he or she died, it happened, it's over.
The whole village knows; Masculine noun for a village, or a people as a nation.
Has anyone come?; past participle of venir (the -ed form, pairs with haber), meaning come toward the speaker.
Enough problems already!; bastar in the present, for he/she/it — said on its own to mean that is enough.
One step at a time; Masculine noun for a step or pace.
We should talk about this; deber as the would-form, for we — a polite way to suggest something.
I like this music; Feminine noun for music, and also sheet music or a band's sound.

We're going to find out the truth; the plain form of averiguar, to find something out by asking or digging.
I'm afraid of flying; the plain form of volar, to fly or to blow something up.
Will your father come?; venir in the future, for he/she/it — to come, built on the stem vendr-.
He ran out of the house; the -ing form of correr, as in salir corriendo meaning to rush out.
I'm still going to class; the -ing form of ir, meaning going and used after seguir for continuing.
My daughter goes to school; Masculine noun for a primary or secondary school often private.
It doesn't make a sound; Masculine noun for a sound and the volume on a device.
He's a real gentleman; Masculine noun for a gentleman and the label on a men's room.
I don't know the code; Masculine noun for a code from a PIN to a legal code.
What do you want us to do?; hacer in the subjunctive (after wishes, doubt, hopes), for we — also used alone as let's do it.
I can't see the picture; Feminine noun for an image or picture with plural imágenes.
It's not worth the risk; Masculine noun for a risk as in correr un riesgo.
We're home; llegar in the present, for we — to arrive, and this form looks the same as the past.
Is there bread at home?; Masculine noun for bread where un pan is a single loaf.
It's worth a million dollars; Masculine noun for a million needing de before the noun counted.
The lady wants to talk to you; Feminine noun for a lady in formal or old-fashioned use.
I want water with ice; Masculine noun for ice as in romper el hielo to break the ice.
He fell in the street; caer in the past, for he/she/it — to fall, it happened and it's over, usually used as caerse.
The press already knows; Feminine noun for the press as a whole and also a press machine.
They avenge his death; vengar in the present, for they — to avenge someone or something.
I'd rather walk; the plain form of caminar, to walk or go on foot.
There's nothing on TV; Feminine noun for television with el televisor for the set itself.
Nothing will happen; pasar in the future, for he/she/it — to happen or to pass.
There are moments like that; Masculine plural of momento as in por el momento meaning for now.
Can I take your car?; the plain form of coger, to take or catch in Spain but vulgar in Latin America.
There's a chance; Feminine noun for a possibility or chance with plural posibilidades.
I wish he had come; haber in the past subjunctive, for he/she/it — past unreal ideas like si hubiese sabido.
That's my seat; Masculine noun for a seat as in tomar asiento meaning have a seat.
The project is finished; Masculine noun for a project or plan.
